content:
Class 5 measurement runs the full metric ladder — mm to km, mg to kg, mL to kL — with decimal conversions. Pure rule-application marks. Here is what the IMO Class 5 measurement chapter tests, with a free 10-question test.

What the Class 5 Maths Olympiad Measurement chapter tests

  • The metric ladder (km hm dam m dm cm mm)
  • Decimal conversions between units
  • Operations on measures (with carrying between units)
  • Choosing sensible units and word problems

Key facts your child should know

  • Each ladder step = × 10 down, ÷ 10 up.
  • 1 km = 1000 m; 1 kg = 1000 g; 1 L = 1000 mL; 1 kL = 1000 L.
  • 2.75 km = 2750 m; 4380 g = 4.38 kg.
  • Convert to the SAME unit before adding or comparing.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Multiplying when you should divide in conversions.
  • Adding mixed units without converting.
  • Slipping a zero in ×1000 conversions.

quiz.title: IMO Class 5 Measurement Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: A volleyball net stretches 12 m 5 cm tall. What is this length in centimetres?
A bus route has two legs of 3 km 750 m and then 4 km 850 m. What is the total distance?
A silver bar weighs 2 kg. What is this mass in milligrams?
A schoolboy jogs 3 km 600 m in 20 minutes. Find his speed in metres per minute.
A glass holds 425 mL of lemonade. How much lemonade is needed to fill 8 such glasses? Answer in litres and millilitres.
A canteen shares 9 L 100 mL of soup equally among 7 tureens. How much soup goes into each tureen?
A fruit vendor had 8 kg 500 g of mangoes and sold 5 kg 675 g. How much is left?
A mountain tunnel is 6 km long. What is this length in centimetres?
questions.explanation: 6 km = 6,000 m. Since 1 m = 100 cm, the length is 6,000 × 100 = 6,00,000 cm.

questions.q: A bag of jaggery weighs 3 kg 750 g. What is this mass in milligrams?
A school bus route is 2 km 450 m one way. How far does the bus travel in 5 one-way trips?

faq.q: How many metres are in 2.75 km?
faq.a: 2750 m — multiply by 1000 when going from kilometres to metres.
4.38 kg, or 4 kg 380 g — divide by 1000.
